Zacharia, whom President Donald Trump named Friday as successor to Karoline Leavitt appeared in the briefing room for the first time on just her second day on the job . She opened by telling reporters she was “so honored” to be working for Trump and noted that she’d “wanted to work for him for a very long time.” She spent the next six minutes reading haltingly from prepared remarks replete with praise for Trump and boasts about purported successes dating back months, including what she called a “historic one-day war” against Venezuela as the actual war Trump started with Iran approaches its ninth month. When it came time to take questions, Zacharia worked from a list of outlets laid out on a note-card that was captured by a photographer’s camera placed above the press secretary’s lectern. She first called on a reporter from the right-wing Breitbart News , who was in a seat normally used by White House staff that her predecessor repurposed for “new media” outlets that are generally friendly to the administration. She then turned to Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy , who asked her if the U.S. has halted sharing intelligence with Ukraine amid Trump’s blow-up at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky . clusters.text: The family of a man who was killed by a tiger after he entered its enclosure at a wildlife park has paid tribute, describing him as "bright, warm and engaging". William Chapman, 23, visited Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday and was attacked after going into the animal's pen. He was pronounced dead at the scene. In a statement, his family said that he had suffered from "significant mental illness" over a number of years and had been prescribed "strong medication". His family added: "It will be for the coroner to decide what part this played in his death. We would ask everybody to respect that process." City of Doncaster Council has launched a health and safety investigation into Chapman's death and the park remains closed. A reopening date has not been confirmed. "William was a bright, warm and engaging young man whom his family dearly loved - and William loved them back," a statement released on Tuesday evening said. The family also asked for privacy, saying "the publication and circulation of deeply offensive media content is causing them severe distress at an exceptionally vulnerable time". "The family are utterly devastated by their loss and are struggling to come to terms with what has happened," the statement continued. "The family are hopeful that the relevant authorities will do their upmost to get to the bottom of why our amazing son did what he did." A spokesperson for the South Yorkshire Police said Chapman's family are being supported by specialist officers. Footage of the incident has been widely shared on social media, including on Tuesday evening by US President Donald Trump. Delhi's Special Executive Magistrate Court remanded Das and Ranka to five days in judicial custody, while Shinde was released on a personal bond. The two leaders can seek bail from a higher court. Yamin Ahmadzai played one of the most crucial knocks. Even though he scored only 19, he soaked up 85 balls. clusters.text: Ranchi police have registered a case against five people, including four members of a family, for allegedly assaulting a Dalit woman, using casteist slurs against her and preventing her from drawing water from their well. clusters.text: Sonay Kartal reached a career-high ranking of 44 following Wimbledon last year Britain's Sonay Kartal upset ninth seed Belinda Bencic as she continued to build post-injury momentum at the Wuhan Open. Kartal reached a career-high ranking of 44 last year but has slipped to 170th in the world after a six-month injury absence. Having returned to action for Great Britain at last month's Billie Jean King Cup Finals, the 24-year-old reached the third round at the Beijing Open last week before beating Ukraine's Anhelina Kalinina in her opening match in Wuhan. The impressive 6-0 7-5 victory over Swiss world number 12 Bencic, a Wimbledon semi-finalist last year, was the second biggest win of Kartal's career by ranking. "I trusted that I would be able to get my level back, I just didn't know how quickly," Kartal said. "I did a lot of things right today but I still think there's a long way to go. "I can produce the level, but can I sustain it? I think that's going to be the hardest challenge. I'm happy to be back, I'm feeling good." Kartal will face Italian 15th seed Jasmine Paolini or 20-year-old Czech Nikola Bartunkova for a quarter-final place. Kartal suffered a stress fracture in her back in March, which meant she missed three of this year's four Grand Slams - including Wimbledon. The Briton, who reached the fourth round at her home Slam last year, was in good form before that enforced break. That included victories over American top-20 seeds Emma Navarro and Madison Keys at Indian Wells, before she retired against Elena Rybakina in the third round with the back issue. Kartal has made a positive return, beating Chinese 31st seed Wang Xinyu as she reached the third round in Beijing, and has now won four of her five matches on her return to the WTA Tour. Former world number one Iga Swiatek also progressed, recording her 40th win of the season with a 6-2 6-1 victory over fellow Pole Magdalena Frech.

clusters.text: Prayagraj: Holding that an applicant cannot be penalised for delays attributable to the postal system, the Allahabad high court has ruled that a candidate who applied online and dispatched the hard copy of the application within the prescribed period cannot be excluded from the selection process merely because it reached the recruiting authority after the cut-off date.In this backdrop, Justice Manju Rani Chauhan directed the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) to accept the hard copy submitted by the petitioner by Oct 16 and consider her candidature for recruitment in the medical education department of UP.“The recruiting authority, having itself prescribed and sanctioned transmission through registered post speed post cannot, in the same breath, disown the consequences of that very mode of transmission and visit an otherwise diligent candidate with the drastic civil consequence of exclusion from the selection process,” the court observed.Through an advertisement dated Aug 18, applications were invited for posts under the medical education department to be filled solely through interviews. The online application and fee were to be submitted by Sept 1, while the hard copy of the application along with requisite documents had to reach the commission by 5 pm on Sept 15, through registered post, speed post or by hand.The petitioner applied online and paid the fee on Aug 31, and sent the hard copy by registered post on Sept 8. It reached the commission’s office in Prayagraj on Sept 16, 2026, a day after the cut-off date, and was refused with an endorsement to that effect on the envelope, which was returned to the petitioner on Sept 21.The postal authorities informed the petitioner that offices in Delhi New Delhi had remained closed from Sept 11-13, on account of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit. clusters.text: NEW DELHI: The Education Ministry on Tuesday announced that it has constituted a three-member committee to examine all details pertaining to the recent death of a student at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT) in the Ranchi campus.Prof. Rajni Abbi, Director, South Campus, University of Delhi, will head the committee, with a senior psychiatrist and a senior officer from the education ministry appointed as members.Aditya Singh, a first-year student of the institute, was found dead in his hostel room on Saturday (Oct 10). Protests erupted on campus in its aftermath. Nearly 1,000 students took to the streets on Monday to protest the death and demand better infrastructure at the campus."The Committee has been mandated to examine the circumstances surrounding the incident and assess the implementation of the guidelines, with particular reference to the availability and functioning of basic facilities, institutional support systems, counselling and mentoring arrangements, and student grievance redressal mechanisms," an official release said. The team will identify systemic gaps and recommend measures to strengthen student well-being and help prevent such incidents from recurring, it added.The Committee shall interact with stakeholders and examine relevant records and documents as required.The Ministry added that it was undertaking suitable interim administrative arrangements to ensure the Institute's smooth and effective functioning, keeping in view the interests and well-being of the students..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

clusters.title: Soil health cards reveal nutrient deficiency in Prayagraj agricultural fields | Hindustan Times
clusters.text: Low levels of organic carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus have become a concern in agricultural soils across Prayagraj, with soil health card tests indicating a decline in natural soil fertility, officials of the regional soil testing laboratory said.The findings have prompted the agriculture department to intensify efforts to promote balanced nutrient use, organic farming and water conservation among farmers to preserve soil health and sustain crop productivity.As part of the campaign to assess soil quality, 77,800 soil health cards have been prepared in Prayagraj so far. These include 23,000 cards in 2024, 46,000 in 2025 and 8,800 in the current financial year. Officials said the target of preparing 8,800 cards for the current kharif season was achieved in October.Piyush Rai, assistant director at the Regional Soil Testing Laboratory in Prayagraj, said the tests covered 12 parameters. Six parameters were examined at soil testing centres established in the district’s five tehsils, while the remaining six were analysed at the soil conservation laboratory at the district headquarters.“The test results show that organic carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus levels are considerably below the desired range in several cases. The decline in organic carbon is particularly concerning as it affects soil structure, moisture retention and the ability to supply nutrients to crops,” Rai said.Organic carbon plays a crucial role in maintaining soil structure, supporting beneficial microorganisms and retaining moisture. According to officials, soil containing around 560 kg of organic carbon per hectare is considered good, while levels between 280 kg and 560 kg per hectare fall in the medium category.Rai said the average organic carbon content in Prayagraj’s soil has been found to be below the medium category.A decline in organic carbon can make soil hard and crusted, restrict the movement of air and water, and reduce its ability to retain moisture and nutrients. It can also affect earthworms and beneficial soil bacteria that contribute to soil fertility.Officials are also focusing on the excessive and imbalanced use of chemical fertilisers in the pursuit of higher yields.
